in_short: The recorded values are systematically too high or too low compared with the true ones, because of how the data is collected or recorded.
The data does not adequately represent part of the population, so results are worse for those who are under-represented.
The data carries assumptions, standards or circumstances of the past that no longer fit the present.
The data selected does not representatively capture the full range of the domain.
Groups that differ are combined as if they were alike, so the result fits the largest group and overlooks smaller ones.
The labels reflect the subjective judgement of the people who assigned them.
Outcomes are identified or verified with different methods or intensity for different groups.
A system's outputs come back as its future inputs, so an early skew is preserved or magnified.
Important information was removed or left out of the data, leaving blind spots.
People favour the output of an automated system over their own judgement or other evidence.
